basis.text: The licence looked up is ABC Type 48 (on-sale general, public premises), as stated in the description.

A Type 48 licence is an on-sale general licence. State law limits these to one for each 2,000 inhabitants of the county; in a county over that number ABC issues no additional one, so the licence comes by transfer of an existing licence unless state law allows otherwise.
Census tract 106.00: 52 active on-sale retail licences in ABC's licences as they stood on 16 March 2022, against 12 authorised in ABC's census tract authorisations of September 2026.

The tract is over its authorised number. State law tests a new licence and a transfer from other premises for undue concentration, and the applicant does not say how the liquor licence will be obtained.

filing_playbook.action: Obtain a written zoning determination from the San Francisco Planning Department on whether a Conditional Use Authorization is required for a bar use at 270 Columbus Ave and whether formula retail applies.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Submit a letter or email to the Planning Department Zoning Administrator describing the concept (bar, full liquor, limited kitchen, no entertainment, closing before midnight, existing restaurant or vacant space). Ask: (1) Is a Conditional Use Authorization required under Planning Code Section 714 for a bar use on the first story and basement? (2) If the business is part of a chain, does formula retail conditional use apply? (3) What is the status of the 1985 conditional use Motion 10438 referenced in the 2002 approval—does it still govern the space? Request a written response citing code sections and case law.
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Form the legal entity with the California Secretary of State (LLC or corporation) and obtain an Employer Identification Number from the IRS, then register the business with the San Francisco Treasurer & Tax Collector to receive a Business Account Number.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: File Articles of Organization (LLC-1, $70) or Articles of Incorporation (ARTS-GS, $100) online. Within 90 days, file the Statement of Information ($20 LLC, $25 corporation). Apply for an EIN (free, issued immediately). With the EIN and entity documents, register online with the SF Treasurer; the fee is tiered by gross receipts (for example, $55 up to $100k, each plus a $4 state fee).
filing_playbook.verification_note: Cut down to the part the cited record states.

filing_playbook.action: Apply for the San Francisco Department of Public Health Permit to Operate a food facility online at least one month before the planned opening.
filing_playbook.what_to_say: Create an account with your Business Account Number, Location ID, and EIN. One owner or employee must pass an ANSI-accredited food safety manager certification exam (ServSafe or equivalent, about $125–$200) within 60 days of opening. Pay the $470 Permit to Operate application fee (includes initial inspection). DPH will schedule a final inspection before issuing the permit. Do not serve the public before the permit is issued.

timeline_cost.notes: The timeline and cost cover the Conditional Use Authorization, the ABC Type 48 license transfer, the health permit, and the building permit with change-of-use review, assuming all are approved. The day range (134–360 days) is the time from filing the CUA to obtaining all approvals when they are granted: CUA 120–300 days, ABC transfer (if unprotested in an over-concentrated tract with PCN review) 90–180 days overlapping with the CUA, health permit 14–45 days, and building permit (if needed) 14–120 days. The CUA and ABC transfer run in parallel after the CUA is approved, so the longer of the two sets the critical path. The cost range ($20,775–$467,400) includes CUA application fee $3,100–$15,000, ABC license purchase and transfer $17,000–$450,000 (the license itself, not a government fee, dominates the range), health permit $470–$1,000, building permit $800–$15,000 if tenant improvements are needed, business registration $55–$700, entity formation $70–$150, and seller's permit $0. It does not include construction costs, rent, or operating expenses. The timeline assumes approval; a CUA denial, a withdrawn application, or an ABC transfer denial would end the process without opening, and no time to a denial or withdrawal is estimated here. Confirm the formula retail status and obtain a written zoning determination from Planning before beginning the ABC license search, because if a CUA is not required the timeline shortens by 4–10 months and the cost drops by $3,000–$15,000.

records_summary: 270 Columbus Ave sits in the Broadway Neighborhood Commercial District (NCD-BROADWAY) where a Bar use on the first story and basement is a conditional use requiring Planning Commission approval. The site history shows continuous bar and restaurant operations since at least 2002, with a fast-food restaurant conditional use approved in 1985, followed by multiple approvals for full bar and full-service restaurant uses, and a Place of Entertainment permit approved in 2006. The block is extremely dense: 49 registered food and drink businesses within 500 ft (18 of them bars), 33 active on-sale ABC licenses within 500 ft, and 106 licenses within 1,000 ft, triggering ABC's undue-concentration flag.
